title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The government says it agrees with the Committee’s 2020 findings that clear rules, transparency and public trust are crucial for safe AI use. It outlines plans to review existing standards, improve oversight, and work with industry and citizens to create a trustworthy AI environment.

title: EM on EU Regulation 2024/1689 on Artificial Intelligence
description: The government's summary of an EU regulation laying down harmonised rules on artificial intelligence and amending several Regulations and Directives.
summary: This document explains the EU’s new Regulation 2024/1689, which establishes unified rules for the development and use of artificial intelligence across member states. It revises and amends several existing regulations and directives to promote safer, more transparent, and accountable AI technologies.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual is setting rules to manage how artificial intelligence can be used in exams and qualifications, making sure it doesn’t compromise fairness or the integrity of the test results. The policy outlines guidelines and standards that schools, exam bodies, and students must follow when using AI tools in the assessment process.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: This report examines how copyrighted works are used in training AI systems and evaluates the legal and societal impacts. It offers recommendations to balance copyright protection with innovation in AI development.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The UK government has issued a formal reply to the House of Lords Select Committee’s report on artificial intelligence, titled “AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency.” In its response, it outlines how it plans to tackle the report’s recommendations and strengthen the country’s AI strategy and regulatory framework.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: This document outlines the scope, objectives, and responsibilities for a committee tasked with reviewing how artificial intelligence should align with public standards. It also includes FAQs to clarify key points and guide stakeholders on the committee’s process.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL has provided written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee’s inquiry into how artificial intelligence is governed, offering its perspective on current policies and practices. The submission aims to help shape future regulatory frameworks for AI by highlighting concerns, best‑practice recommendations, and potential areas for improvement.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: AI is reshaping how medical products are regulated, requiring new safety and effectiveness standards that account for AI technologies. This policy will implement the AI White Paper principles to guide the updated regulatory framework.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy aims to make the Defence organisation the most effective, efficient, trusted, and influential AI user among similarly sized entities. It focuses on developing advanced AI capabilities, establishing strong governance, and building partnerships to support national security objectives.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport Artificial Intelligence Action Plan outlines how the Department for Transport will partner with the transport sector to harness the benefits of AI while mitigating associated risks. It details strategies for collaboration, governance, and implementation to support innovation while safeguarding public safety and trust.
